entities.summary:
Íñigo Fernández de Velasco, 2nd Duke of Frías, Grandee of Spain, and Constable of Castile, represented the pinnacle of Castilian noble power during a pivotal era of Spanish history, spanning his birth in 1462 to his death on September 17, 1528. As head of the illustrious House of Velasco, one of the wealthiest and most influential lineages in the Kingdom of Castile, he wielded significant political, military, and economic authority across Southern Europe. His life intersected directly with the reigns of the Catholic Monarchs, Ferdinand II and Isabella I, and their grandson, Emperor Charles V, positioning him as a crucial figure in the transition from medieval feudalism to the centralized monarchy of early modern Spain.

His career was marked by unwavering loyalty to the Crown, particularly during periods of intense internal strife. Fernández de Velasco participated prominently in the War of the Castilian Succession (1475–1479), supporting Isabella I against Joanna la Beltraneja, a conflict that solidified the Trastámara dynasty. Later, as Constable of Castile, a hereditary office granting supreme military command, he played a decisive role in suppressing the Revolt of the Comuneros (1520–1522), leading royalist forces to victory at the Battle of Villalar in April 1521. This triumph crushed noble and urban resistance, irrevocably strengthening the monarchy's authority over its territories and subjects. He also served as Viceroy of Galicia, extending his administrative reach.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Íñigo Fernández de Velasco was a pivotal figure in the consolidation of royal power in Castile, particularly through his decisive role in suppressing the Revolt of the Comuneros, which fundamentally reshaped the relationship between the monarchy and its subjects. His actions ensured the stability of the nascent Spanish imperial project and solidified the enduring influence of the great noble houses.
